== Problem ==

If <imath>n</imath> is an even positive integer, the <imath>\emph{double factorial}</imath> notation <imath>n!!</imath> represents the product of all the even integers from <imath>2</imath> to <imath>n</imath>. For example, <imath>8!! = 2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 \cdot 8</imath>. What is the units digit of the following sum? <cmath>2!! + 4!! + 6!! + \cdots + 2018!! + 2020!! + 2022!!</cmath>

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 0\qquad\textbf{(B) } 2\qquad\textbf{(C) } 4\qquad\textbf{(D) } 6\qquad\textbf{(E) } 8</imath>

== Solution 1 ==

Notice that once <imath>n>8,</imath> the units digit of <imath>n!!</imath> will be <imath>0</imath> because there will be a factor of <imath>10.</imath> Thus, we only need to calculate the units digit of <cmath>2!!+4!!+6!!+8!! = 2+8+48+48\cdot8.</cmath> We only care about units digits, so we have <imath>2+8+8+8\cdot8,</imath> which has the same units digit as <imath>2+8+8+4.</imath> The answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}.</imath>

~wamofan

==Solution 2 (Solution 1 worded differently)==

We can see that after <imath>8!!</imath> in the sequence, the units digit is always <imath>0</imath> (every value after <imath>8!!</imath> is a multiple of <imath>10</imath>). Therefore, our answer is the sum of the units digits of <imath>2!!, 4!!, 6!!,</imath> and <imath>8!!</imath> respectively. This sum is equal to <imath>2 + 8 + 8 + 4</imath>, or <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 2}.</imath>

~Irfans123
